text:
Alex Chen: Hey folks — quick scenario. Partner accepted a role in Portugal and we're planning to move with our 3yo in ~8 weeks. I'm currently on paid parental leave until 2026-05-20. Questions: do I need to change home base immediately? How will switching impact my WFH stipend proration, 401(k) match, HSA contributions, and continuity of parental leave/health benefits? Also curious about payroll cutover timelines and whether Redwood offers any shipping/relocation help for a personal move.
Priya (People Ops): Congrats on the move! Short answers first: changing home base affects payroll & benefits, so timing matters. WFH stipend proration depends on the homebase effective date; 401(k) match and HSA are tied to US payroll/eligibility and may cease if you switch off US payroll; parental leave typically continues if you're still a Redwood employee on our payroll. We'll need to coordinate with Benefits and Payroll for specifics.
Olivia (Benefits): @Alex, a few clarifying Qs: will you remain on Redwood US payroll for an interim period or plan to switch to a local arrangement right away? If you stay on US payroll and keep a US mailing address, you can often keep benefits for a short period but network access in Portugal will be limited and some providers won't cover out-of-country care. HSA eligibility requires being enrolled in a US-qualified HDHP and filing US taxes — contributions may not be allowed while living abroad. Recommend contacting Fidelity and submitting the benefits case so we can advise next steps.
Ben (Payroll): Hi Alex — payroll cutovers require ~6 weeks lead time. If you elect to change home base to Portugal, Payroll will either cut over to local payroll/EO or maintain US payroll temporarily depending on legal/immigration status. Please fill out the Homebase Change form: https://redwood.internal/payroll/homebase-change with your proposed effective date so we can model taxes and withholding.
Alex Chen: Thanks. I'm hoping to stay on Redwood payroll for 60–90 days to get settled. My partner's start date is 2026-06-15 and we're aiming to move around 2026-06-20. If I stay on US payroll, will parental leave pay continue through that 90-day window?
Priya (People Ops): If you remain employed by Redwood and on our payroll, paid parental leave continues per policy. If you change employment (e.g., switch to a local employer or local payroll), that can terminate eligibility. We'll mark this as high priority because of your current leave status — we don't want any interruption. Please DM me the exact move date and confirm the 'stay on US payroll' preference.
Alex Chen: Also, we have a big desk and car seat to ship. Is there any relocation assistance or one-off reimbursement for personal moves?
Olivia (Benefits): We don't have a standard relocation package for voluntary family moves. We can approve exceptional reimbursements on a case-by-case basis if pre-approved by People Ops and finance. For shipping/temporary housing reimbursements: submit an expense request in Concur and tag it with "homebase-move" after you get Priya's approval.
Ben (Payroll): For the WFH stipend: if your homebase change effective date is within the month, stipend will be prorated for that month. We'll include that in the payroll model when you submit the form. 401(k) match will stop when you stop contributing through US payroll. We can run a projection showing the delta for 60/90-day US payroll retention vs immediate cutover.
Priya (People Ops): Next steps summary: 1) Alex, submit the Homebase Change form and indicate you'd like to remain on US payroll for ~90 days. 2) Olivia will open a benefits case to check plan portability and HSA/health implications. 3) Ben will run payroll cutover scenarios and stipend proration numbers. 4) We'll review relocation reimbursement possibilities and confirm documentation. I'll set up a 30-min sync to walk through.
Alex Chen: Awesome — appreciate the quick turnaround. Can we meet Tue or Wed this week? I'm mostly offline but can jump in a 30m slot.
Priya (People Ops): Sent a calendar invite for Tue 10:00am PT. Invited @Ben and @Olivia. We'll have the initial payroll/benefits checklist ready by then. :thumbsup:
Ben (Payroll): Got it, see you Tue.
Olivia (Benefits): See you then — I'll pull plan details and HSA guidance ahead of the call.
Alex Chen: Thanks everyone — talk soon.
